$schema-note: Checked-in ratchet floors for the third-party coverage study (issue #493). Read and enforced by tools/coverage-study/coverage_table.py, which .github/workflows/coverage-study.yml runs after the seven measuring jobs. A run below any row's floor fails the workflow; a run above it raises the floor here and the bot commits the raise, so a gain cannot be given back silently. Seeded from the first all-green run of the full seven-job matrix: https://github.com/Ball-Lang/ball/actions/runs/33953210701 (2026-09-05). To re-seed a row deliberately (a changed pin list changes the denominator, which is a breach by design), edit its numbers in a reviewed commit - never widen a floor to make a red run green.
$funnel-note: `encoded`/`compiledBack`/`reencoded`/`declarationsKept` are the four Tier A funnel stages, index for index with the columns of the published table, and EVERY one of them is floored as a ratio against `scored` - the same ratchet the clean ratio carries. Before issue #632 only `encoded` (stage 1) was, which left the one stage whose INPUT is this repository's own output unguarded: stages 1 and 2 read third-party source and the Ball IR encoded from it, while stage 3 re-encodes what this project's compiler just emitted, so a construct the compiler emits that its own encoder refuses shows up there and nowhere else. That is exactly what #632 was - rust/compiler's method-dispatcher `panic!` arm, refused by rust/encoder - and no gate in the repository could see it. The funnel is monotone, so each stage's floor also fails when an earlier one regresses; the stages are floored separately anyway, because WHERE a row stopped is the whole signal on a pipeline whose round trip is not closed, and a trade (stage 1 up, stage 3 down) must not net out to silence. The three stages added here were seeded from the artifacts of https://github.com/Ball-Lang/ball/actions/runs/34769384905 (2026-09-13), read through coverage_table.py's own `measure()` rather than typed, and every one of them equals the number the table already published from an earlier run.
$excluded-note: `excluded` is RECORDED, NOT FLOORED. It is the count of test-only files each Tier A harness takes OUT of the denominator, per that language's own convention (the owner's 2026-09-14 methodology decision on issue #491: Tier A scores the library code a user would encode, and a package's own test suite is a different population). It is not a quality measure - a pin whose own test suite grew moves it up, one that dropped a test moves it down, and neither is a regression - so no floor is applied to it. It lives here so that a ratio which moved because an exclusion RULE moved is visible in the committed diff rather than only inside a job log. A Tier A artifact that carries NO count is a hard failure in coverage_table.py, and summarize.sh fails the job on a missing `excluded (test-only): N` line, because a harness whose rule silently vanished would otherwise publish a denominator nobody can account for. ONE shape of movement IS a breach (#648): a drop to 0 from a baseline above it while `scored` rises by at least that many files means the whole excluded population re-entered the denominator - an exclusion RULE that stopped firing, which no ratio floor can see (the denominator grew, and the readmitted files may well be clean). That is reported with that cause and does NOT raise the row; the same drop with an unchanged denominator is still an ordinary raise.
$python-reseed-note: The Python row was re-seeded on 2026-09-21 (issue #721) to `scored 70, encoded 2, compiledBack 2, reencoded 2, declarationsKept 2`, measured over the same four pins with the fixed harness. Three of those five move DOWN, and the reason is a denominator that was never stable rather than a pipeline that got worse. The old 73 counted `pyparsing/ai/__init__.py`, `ai/show_best_practices/__init__.py` and `tools/__init__.py` - all ZERO-BYTE package markers. rq1_study_py.py used to decide 'no declarations, not scored' at stage 4, AFTER encode/compile-back/re-encode, so those three were scored only while they happened to FAIL at stage 3; #646 made them stop failing and they left the denominator silently, taking `encoded` 5 -> 2 with them. The skip is now taken from the source at stage 0, so the same three leave deterministically and the PRE-#646 artifact (run 34788637747) re-reads as `2/70` as well: the floors above and below this line measure the same corpus the same way. `reencoded`/`declarationsKept` 0 -> 2 is the encoder half of #721 (module-level variables are encoded as declarations instead of being folded into the synthesised main), and those two ratchet from here.
$rust-stage1-note: The Rust row's `encoded`/`compiledBack` were raised 7 -> 9 on 2026-09-21 (issue #767), measured over the SAME five pins and the same checkouts, before and after, with one binary - the `before` reproduced this row's previous numbers exactly (7/7/1/0, excluded 34), which is what makes the `after` a comparison rather than a fresh reading. Two stage-1 gaps closed: tuple expressions (rust/encoder's `encode_tuple` -> std.record) and an `impl` whose self type is a REFERENCE to a named type (types.rs::type_short_name looks through `&T`/`&mut T`). The first-blocker histogram is exactly conserved at 77: `unsupported Rust expression kind `tuple`` 6 -> 0 and `unsupported `impl` self type` 8 -> 4, with every one of those ten files landing on a further gap. `reencoded` stays at 1 and is NOT raised: the two files that newly reached stage 3 both stop on ``unsupported runtime helper `ball_arg_get(...)` ``, the compiled parameter prologue tracked separately as issue #790 - stage 3 is dammed by that helper, not by stage 1, so closing more stage-1 gaps cannot move it until #790 does. Say that rather than implying the funnel moved further than it did.
$reseeded-note: The Rust row was re-seeded on 2026-09-14 for that decision: `scored` 110 -> 77, because 34 of the 119 .rs files under the pinned crates' studied subtrees are bitflags' own tests (33 under `src/tests/`, plus `src/tests.rs`, which only the cfg(test)-reachability half of the rule can see). `clean` and `encoded` are unchanged in absolute terms, so both ratios rose. No other row's denominator moved: TypeScript, Python and Go already filtered their test files - silently, with no count printed anywhere, which is what this change ends.
